version_note: Verifier revision 2 of 2026-09-16 (still 0.0.6), a review of every time comparison: (a) the two places where an implementation timestamp is compared against the verifier's own Date.now() reading (the run start of the first case, the shutdown window) now allow 1 ms below, matching the 1 ms already allowed above; (b) the two comparisons that mix clocks inside the trace, a turn start (pinned by the contract to pi's millisecond event timestamp) against the previous turn's sub-millisecond end in the steering case, and a child process's run against the parent's tool span in the sub-agent case, are made at millisecond granularity like the shared invariants in at_support.ts already were; every other comparison is between two timestamps of one implementation clock and stays exact; found when the claude-opus-5 submission, whose clock is a monotonic hrtime offset anchored on a millisecond-truncated Date.now() (an OpenTelemetry-style clock the instruction permits: 'sub-millisecond digits are yours'), failed the shutdown case in 2 of 8 local runs by 16 microseconds while passing in Harbor. Verifier revision of 2026-09-16 (still 0.0.6, contract text unchanged): the tool and compaction attribute maps are now checked like the chat map already was, listed keys with the right values and extra keys allowed (toMatchObject instead of toEqual), and the failed-compaction case asserts explicitly that no entry-derived attribute is present; prompted by grok run 11, whose compaction line carried two extra pi.usage.cache_* attributes. 0.0.6 adds one sentence to the failure-safe requirement (a shutdown close carries every attribute known at that moment; an entry id is known only once pi persisted the entry) after the 0.0.5 grok rollout closed pi.run with no attributes; verifier, oracle and controls unchanged, so the 0.0.5 matrix results carry over. 0.0.5 rewrites the instruction as outcome requirements plus an export contract, dropping every prescribed mechanism, and makes the verifier mechanism-agnostic (same Oracle, same controls); 0.0.4 added overflow recovery (error chat, overflow compaction with will_retry, retry run with pi.run.after_compaction) and sub-agent trace propagation through PI_AGENT_TRACE_PARENT, with two contract cases and three controls; 0.0.3 added concurrent tool spans, steering bookkeeping (pi.run.steer_count / steer_entry_ids) and compaction usage accounting with two contract cases and three controls; 0.0.2 added live start lines (every span written at start and at end) and the failure-path requirements (aborted stream, failed compaction, quit while streaming, unwritable path, crash during a tool execution) with five contract cases, one lifecycle case and six controls.

Two genuine defects, both reproduced locally from agent-changes.patch in the task image (~/ai-infra-scratch/repro-run8/repro.log, trace dumps included) and both against explicit instruction text: (1) concurrent tool calls: the extension stamps a tool's end time at tool_execution_end but defers the end line until the tool-result entry id resolves; pi persists parallel tool results after Promise.all in call order, so the 300 ms call's end line (line 7) was written before the 100 ms call's (line 8, earlier endTimeUnixNano); instruction: 'end lines appear in the order the spans ended: endTimeUnixNano never decreases' (the oracle collects tool ends and writes them at turn_end in end order); (2) shutdown: onShutdown closes pi.run with an empty attribute list, so the end line has no pi.run.turn_count and no pi.session.entry_id although pi had persisted the user message (the exemption covers only entries pi never persisted; the oracle resolves the entry id and sets turn_count before closing). Judge correct (expected 0)

real_agent_rollouts.assessment: task 0.0.6 (contract-only + shutdown attribute sentence), first rollout: agent finished in 34 min, no 401s, P2P pass; contract 10/15, lifecycle 1/2. All six failures reproduced locally from agent-changes.patch in the task image (~/ai-infra-scratch/repro-run8/repro9.log) and trace back to three genuine defects, none a judge issue: (a) four cases (manual/threshold, failed compaction, overflow, lifecycle reload) fail because every compaction is exported twice: onCompact first runs ingest(), which sees the persisted compaction entry and closes the open pi.compaction span with its entry id, then finds this.compaction empty, starts a second span and closes it with the same entry id (2 ns apart), so one entry is referenced by two spans; (b) the shutdown case now carries pi.run.turn_count and the run's entry id (the 0.0.6 sentence had its effect) but the streaming chat is closed with pendingChat.endTimeUnixNano, a placeholder initialised to the span's start time and only updated at message_end, so its close lands 300 ms before the verifier's dispose() window (instruction: timestamps come from the clock at the moment of the event); (c) the concurrent case writes tool end lines in persistence order and keeps endTimeUnixNano non-decreasing by clamping (endNano: nano <= lastEnd -> lastEnd + 1), so the 100 ms call's end time is rewritten to the 300 ms call's end + 1 ns and its duration becomes 306 ms (the mirror image of run 8, which kept true times but wrote out of order; the oracle buffers until turn_end and writes in end order with true times). Judge correct (expected 0)
real_agent_rollouts.label: grok run 9

real_agent_rollouts.assessment: task 0.0.6, third rollout, agent timeout multiplier 0.15: agent finished in 25 min, no 401s, P2P pass; contract 12/15, lifecycle 2/2. Reproduced from agent-changes.patch in the task image (~/ai-infra-scratch/repro-run8/repro11.log). Two of the three failures are one genuine defect: the chat span's assistant entry lookup never marks the entry it used, so in the steering case all three chats reference the same assistant entry (706e4480 x3) and in the wakeup/continuation case the fourth chat reuses the third's entry; the branch is not covered exactly once. The third failure is a verifier-strictness finding, not an agent error: the compaction end line carried pi.usage.cache_read_tokens and pi.usage.cache_write_tokens (0, taken from the compaction entry's usage) in addition to the seven attributes the table lists, and the verifier compares the compaction attribute map with toEqual (also for tool spans, lines 158/260/377), while the instruction never says the table is exhaustive. Reward would be 0 regardless because of the entry defect (expected 0), but the exact-match assertions should be relaxed to the listed keys, or the instruction should state that no other attributes are allowed, before more rollouts Re-verified under the revised verifier (2026-09-16, listed-keys matching): contract 13/15, only the two entry-bookkeeping cases fail; reward unchanged at 0.
real_agent_rollouts.label: grok run 11

real_agent_rollouts.agent: claude-code (Harbor built-in, OAuth token) claude-opus-5, agent timeout multiplier 0.15
real_agent_rollouts.assessment: task 0.0.6 (contract-only + shutdown sentence, revised verifier), claude-opus-5 through Harbor's claude-code agent (fresh setup-token, multiplier 0.15): passes every layer unmodified in 28 min (contract 15/15, lifecycle 2/2, P2P pass), 156 turns, 62 Bash calls, no rate-limit pressure (5-hour window at 1%). The first non-curated pass of the contract-only instruction: it resolves entry ids by scanning the branch backwards from its end, lists steering entries per turn, and closes spans on session_shutdown with their attributes. Kept as validation/alt-opus-run1.patch (expected 1) Post-hoc scrutiny (2026-09-16): trajectory reviewed (only the extension directory, its README, the examples README and one new test file were written; the agent ran pi's own suite, tsgo and biome itself; no verifier or node_modules access), traces dumped for the hard cases (true end times, end order kept, shutdown closes carry the run attributes). Repeating the shutdown case locally exposed a verifier over-precision: the submission's hrtime-anchored clock reads up to 1 ms behind Date.now(), and the verifier's window lower bound was exact to the nanosecond, so the case failed 2 of 8 local repeats by 16 us. Fixed in verifier revision 2 (1 ms slack); after the fix 10/10 repeats and 3 full-suite runs pass. The Harbor pass stands, but under revision 1 it carried roughly a one-in-four chance of a spurious 0
real_agent_rollouts.label: opus 2 (0.0.6)
